subject: ela
intro: The main idea is the most important point a passage is trying to teach. It is what the whole passage is mostly about. Key details are the smaller facts and examples that support, or help prove, the main idea. To find the main idea, ask, "What is this mostly about?" Then check that the details all connect to it. A good main idea is not too big and not too small. It covers the whole passage, not just one sentence.

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

Penguins have many ways to stay warm in the icy cold. They have a thick layer of fat under their skin. Their feathers are packed tightly to keep out water and wind. Penguins also huddle close together in big groups to share body heat.

What is the main idea of this passage?

steps: Ask, "What is this mostly about?"
Every detail tells a way penguins stay warm: fat, tight feathers, and huddling.
So the main idea covers all three details.
solution.answer: The main idea is that penguins have many ways to stay warm in the cold. The details about fat, tight feathers, and huddling all support this.

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

The library is a busy place. Children come to check out picture books and hear stories at story time. Older students use computers to do their homework. Adults borrow novels and read the newspaper. There is something for everyone.

What is the main idea, and name two details that support it.

steps: Ask what the passage is mostly about: how the library serves many people.
The main idea sentence is close to "There is something for everyone."
Two supporting details: children hear stories, and older students use computers for homework.
solution.answer: The main idea is that the library has something for everyone. Two supporting details: children hear stories at story time, and older students use computers for homework.

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

Recycling helps our planet in important ways. When we recycle paper, fewer trees are cut down. Recycling cans and bottles means we dig up less new metal and make less new plastic. Recycling also means less trash goes into big landfills.

Which sentence best states the main idea?

steps: Look for the sentence that covers the whole passage.
The first sentence says, "Recycling helps our planet in important ways."
The other sentences are details that give examples of how it helps.
solution.answer: The main idea is the first sentence: "Recycling helps our planet in important ways." The other sentences are details that show how, such as saving trees and making less trash.

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

A dog can be a great helper. Some dogs guide people who cannot see. Other dogs sniff out danger to keep people safe. Farm dogs herd sheep, and rescue dogs find people lost in the snow.

Why is "Dogs herd sheep" NOT a good main idea for this passage?

steps: The main idea must cover the whole passage.
Herding sheep is just one detail, one job among many.
The passage is about many ways dogs help, not only herding.
solution.answer: "Dogs herd sheep" is only one small detail, so it is too small to be the main idea. The main idea is that dogs can be great helpers in many ways.

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

Brushing your teeth is important for many reasons. It cleans away bits of food that can cause holes called cavities. It keeps your gums healthy. Brushing also gives you fresh breath and a bright smile.

What is the main idea of this passage?

steps: Ask what the passage is mostly about.
Every detail gives a reason brushing is important.
The main idea covers all those reasons.
solution.answer: The main idea is that brushing your teeth is important for many reasons. The details name reasons like stopping cavities, keeping gums healthy, and fresh breath.

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

The rain forest is full of life. Colorful birds call from the treetops. Monkeys swing from branch to branch. Frogs, snakes, and thousands of insects live among the plants below. More kinds of animals live here than almost anywhere on Earth.

What is the main idea?

steps: Ask what the whole passage is about.
The details all name animals living in the rain forest.
The last sentence sums it up: many kinds of animals live there.
solution.answer: The main idea is that the rain forest is full of many kinds of animal life. Birds, monkeys, frogs, snakes, and insects are details that support it.

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

Amelia Earhart was a brave pilot. She was the first woman to fly a plane alone across the huge Atlantic Ocean. She set many flying records. She also encouraged other women to become pilots and follow their dreams.

What is the main idea, and give one detail that supports it.

steps: Ask what the passage is mostly about: Amelia Earhart being a brave, important pilot.
The main idea is close to the first sentence.
One supporting detail: she was the first woman to fly alone across the Atlantic Ocean.
solution.answer: The main idea is that Amelia Earhart was a brave and important pilot. One supporting detail: she was the first woman to fly alone across the Atlantic Ocean.

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

Honeybees do much more than make honey. As they move from flower to flower, they carry pollen that helps fruits and vegetables grow. Without bees, we would have far fewer apples, berries, and other foods. Bees are important to the food we eat.

Which detail supports the idea that bees help our food grow?

steps: Find the detail that connects bees to food.
The passage says they "carry pollen that helps fruits and vegetables grow."
That detail supports the main idea.
solution.answer: The detail that bees "carry pollen that helps fruits and vegetables grow" supports the idea that bees help our food grow.

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

Winter can be hard for wild animals. Food becomes hard to find under the snow. The cold air can be dangerous. Some animals, like bears, sleep through the winter in a deep rest called hibernation. Others, like geese, fly to warmer places until spring.

What is the main idea, and how do the details about bears and geese support it?

steps: Ask what the passage is mostly about: how animals deal with hard winters.
Bears hibernate and geese fly south. Both are ways animals survive winter.
These details support the main idea about surviving the cold season.
solution.answer: The main idea is that animals have ways to survive the hard winter. The details support it by showing two ways: bears hibernate, and geese fly to warmer places.

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

Water is always on the move around our planet. The sun warms lakes and oceans, and some water rises into the air as a gas. Up high, it cools and forms clouds. Then the water falls back down as rain or snow, and the whole trip starts again.

Write the main idea of this passage in your own words, then list one detail that supports it.

steps: Ask what the passage is mostly about: water moving in a repeating cycle.
State it in your own words.
Pick one supporting detail, such as water rising into the air or falling as rain.
solution.answer: Main idea: water keeps moving around the planet in a repeating cycle. Supporting detail: the sun warms water so it rises into the air, and later it falls back as rain or snow.
